readme: Localization evidence for the Pages site, one row per canonical feature. The site localizes through its own COPY table rather than the console boundary, because it is a separate artifact that ships without the renderer. `copyKeys` names the entries a feature depends on; a row is `localized` only when every one of them exists in site/app.js, so this file is checkable against that source rather than asserted. The contract test recomputes every state and fails on any row that disagrees.

language-modes.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result

funny-levels.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
funny-levels.note: The site has a working language mechanism (COPY/copyText, both funny sliders, live vocabulary) but no COPY entry covering this feature, so its copy renders English in every mode. Missing translation, not missing wiring.

dialog-emojis.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
dialog-emojis.note: Covered by COPY keys: dialogEmojisDesc. The dialog-emoji card description carries four English and four Cantonese variants, and every one of the eight states both facts the switch turns on: that the wording is unchanged, and that no button, label or screen-reader name carries a glyph. The checkbox label, the card heading and the live status line are still fixed English.

school-mode.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
school-mode.note: The card ships COPY.schoolDesc with four English and four Cantonese funny levels, wired through data-copy="schoolDesc". None of the eight variants names the mode, deliberately: the name is the reader's to change, so it is written into the heading, the status line and the search keywords at run time instead, and a description that named it could never be renamed with it. The status, suppression and recovery sentences are generated at run time from the chosen name and render in English, which is the only language available while the mode is on.

narration.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
narration.note: The narration card ships COPY.narrationDesc with four English and four Cantonese funny levels, wired through data-copy="narrationDesc". Every level states both facts the card rests on: the narrator is off until it is switched on, and everything it reads is already on screen. The two voice-status lines and the spoken lines themselves are generated at runtime; the spoken lines carry their own en/zh wording at each call site, and are deliberately read from copyLevel() rather than copyText() so no personal-vocabulary replacement can be spoken through a network-backed voice.

changelog-viewer.note: Covered by COPY keys: changelogDesc. The changelog description carries four English and four Cantonese variants, and every one of the eight states the two facts the viewer rests on: each line carries the real commit that made it, and what is exported is exactly what is on screen. The section heading, the control labels and the count, range and problem lines are still fixed English. The entries themselves are deliberately NOT localized and never will be: a change summary is a factual external record of what a release said, and restyling it at a funny level would stop it being a record.

context-menu-shortcuts.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
context-menu-shortcuts.note: COPY.contextMenuHint (the keyboard-route footer) and COPY.contextMenuNoMatch (the empty-filter state) each ship four English and four Cantonese variants, wired through copyText() and, for the footer, a data-copy hook so applyCopy() re-renders it on every language or funny-level change. Voice moves with the slider; the facts never do -- item labels, unavailability reasons, the result count and every printed chord are rendered from the action table and the platform rather than from COPY, so they are English at every level. That is deliberate: a shortcut is a key to press, and translating 'Alt+Shift+L' would be translating a fact.

long-operation-progress.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
long-operation-progress.note: COPY.exportEverythingDesc ships four English and four Cantonese variants, wired to the sliders from the start through the dialog's data-copy="exportEverythingDesc" hook. Voice moves with the slider; three facts never do -- every one of the eight states that one file is written per record set in the single format chosen, that nothing leaves this browser, and that the run names the file being written and the count done. That third fact is what separates a progress report from a spinner, so a variant dropping it would be describing a different feature. The plan sentence, the progress sentence, the decline sentence and the disabled reason are rendered from the run's own numbers rather than from COPY, so they are English at every level; they are a factual report of counts and filenames rather than product prose, and every one of them still passes through applyVocabularyText().

in-context-recovery.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
in-context-recovery.note: Every recovery region opens with COPY.recoveryLead, wired through data-copy="recoveryLead" and rendered by copyText('recoveryLead'), with four English and four Cantonese variants. It is the first key here that is hooked from a runtime element rather than from any page's markup, because a region is built by app.js at the moment a failure happens. The split is deliberate and is checked: the lead line carries voice and nothing else, while every fact -- the heading, the reason the browser gave, the sizes of each store, the labels on the buttons and what each forbidden remedy would cost -- sits in a sibling of it, so no funny level can move one. Those facts are written in English at every level, which is the honest state rather than a finished one: translating them is a second pass and the row stays localized on the strength of the key that exists.

automatic-updates.mechanism: console/site/app.js -- the COPY table (per-key en/zh variants at four funny levels), copyText() as the selector, and applyVocabularyText() over the result
automatic-updates.note: COPY.updatesDesc ships four English and four Cantonese variants, wired to the sliders from the start through the settings card's data-copy="updatesDesc" hook. Voice moves with the slider; four facts never do -- every one of the eight states that the comparison is on the build commit rather than the version label, that nothing installs or downloads in the background, that reloading is what takes the new page, and that the check asks this same site for one small file and sends nothing anywhere. The banner and status wording is rendered from the watch own state rather than from COPY, so it is English at every level; it is a factual report of two build identities rather than product prose, and every string in it still passes through applyVocabularyText().
